name: Opal Felix
episode: The other side of the cove
life: “I still remember the donor who cared more about direction than inscription.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Opal by a small Sunday habit. Opal prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I saved the original donor letter. It specified a sea view and made no mention of who's looking.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a faded indigo overshirt and a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. Opal has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Opal looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Opal talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Opal's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To verify the original gift's view requirement.
family: Lou Reed is Opal’s cousin raised in the same household. Their relatives kept a holiday fund in a boot that still had its mate. Even after the family acquired bank accounts, an envelope of change at supper meant somebody was planning a journey. Opal works out what it costs to bring everybody. Asked about *The release address*, Lou says, “I moved without giving him the new number because I needed one quiet Christmas.”
connections: Vincent Albright. A saved donor letter helps a reluctant walker see how a name could earn its place on the bench.

reactions.situation: A public donor asks to approve the wording on the bench
reactions.response: Opal asks the cleaner and the donor for separate views on the wording.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Opal tells the first helper what they actually saw and makes room for the rider to answer for themself.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Opal says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
